title: Lane Matrix: model & route performance wireflows and chart specs
creator: Samira Patel
description: Goal: design a lane-oriented matrix view that surfaces per-model and per-route performance signals (latency distribution, throughput, token metrics) in a compact, scannable grid. This ticket contains wireflows, chart specs, and prototype links for review with PM/Eng. The lane matrix groups rows by model variant and columns by route (or endpoint tag). Each cell is a self-contained lane with three microcharts: a percentile ribbon for latency (p50/p95/p99 bands), a throughput spark bar for requests/sec over time, and a token density mini-histogram. Cells can expand into an inspector panel with microtraces and recent error samples.
acceptance_criteria: Design review completed with Eng and PM and sign-off recorded in comments
Figma prototype includes: lane matrix layout, expanded inspector state, and interactions for canary vs primary route toggles
Chart specs document lists input data, aggregation windows, and recommended defaults for sampling and downsampling
Accessibility notes cover keyboard navigation between lanes and color contrast for heat/ribbon bands
Hand-off artifact includes component-level tokens, spacing, and responsive rules for narrow consoles
chart_specs: Percentile ribbon: show p50 (center line), shaded p75/p95 bands, and thin p99 outline. Data window default 1h with 1m resolution. Render as stacked translucent layers to preserve token cost overlays.
Throughput spark bar: aggregated requests/sec per 1m bucket. Use microbars with hover to show exact RPS and example request id. Support smoothing toggle (EMA 0.2).
Token density mini-histogram: bucketed token counts per request (0-64,65-128,129-256,257-512,512+). Show percentage stacked bar inside cell and numeric median on hover.
Cell expand interaction: on expand, show microtrace waterfall aligned to percentile ribbon time axis and top 3 error messages sampled.
design_decisions: Use lane matrix grid to maximize vertical scannability for SREs monitoring many model variants simultaneously
Percentile ribbon chosen over violin plots to make distribution changes over time clearer in narrow cells
Minimize tokenized color palette to three hues + grayscale to avoid visual noise and to remain accessible for color-blind users
tradeoffs: Compact lanes sacrifice raw sample count visibility; mitigated by explicit sample count tooltip and inspector mode
Using p99 as thin outline can hide micro-outliers; decision kept to preserve cell simplicity for quick triage
Real-time streaming of all lanes is costly; default to last-1h update cadence with manual refresh and top-5 hot-lanes live streaming option
review_feedback: PM (Ethan Cole): prioritize quick comparison mode to highlight regressions between current and previous rollout baseline
Eng (Marcel Ritter): request explicit data contract for pXX endpoints and downsampling behavior; added action item to draft instrumentation spec
Security (Priya Anand): flagged that expanded inspector must redact PII in sampled request content by default
Accessibility (Amina Shah): recommend keyboard focus ring between cells and ARIA labels for chart elements

Prototype micro-interactions in code sandbox and validate animation perf across chrome and minimal hardware (owner: Lina)

notes_for_engineering: Provide two backend endpoints: /metrics/lane-summary (aggregate p50/p75/p95/p99, rps, median_tokens) and /metrics/lane-timeseries (1m buckets, sample ids)
Recommend using pre-aggregated sliding windows for pXX to keep cell render time < 80ms
Include telemetry events: lane.expanded, lane.hover, lane.compare-baseline to link back to usage analytics
